source: GATE DA Complete PYQ Book (2024 IISc, 2025 IIT Roorkee, 2026 IIT Guwahati), pp. 3-6

subjects.name: Probability & Statistics
subjects.style: Shifted from single-variable calculus to joint distributions, covariance matrices, and Bayes network inference.

subjects.name: Programming, DSA
subjects.style: Stabilised at ~13–15M; evolved from C-style logic to Python internals, mutable defaults, and tree traversals.

subjects.name: General Aptitude
subjects.style: Strictly invariant 15M (5×1M + 5×2M): quantitative puzzles, spatial reasoning, reading comprehension.

subjects.name: Machine Learning
subjects.style: Peaked in 2025 with neural-net backpropagation; stabilised around distance metrics, clustering, and decision trees.

subjects.name: Database Mgmt & Warehousing
subjects.style: Exploded from basic ER modelling to star/snowflake schemas, OLAP operations, and B+ trees.

subjects.name: Linear Algebra
subjects.style: Rock-solid predictability; eigenvalues, null spaces, projections, and matrix rank.

subjects.name: Artificial Intelligence
subjects.style: Heuristic search (A* queue expansion, admissible heuristics) and adversarial game trees.

subjects.name: Calculus & Optimization
subjects.style: Moved from broad multivariable calculus to convex optimisation, gradient-descent steps, and local extrema.

v: Applied ML, neural nets & heuristic search

takeaways: Standard single-choice questions fell from 56.9% (37 Qs) in 2024 to 50.8% (33 Qs) in 2026, shifting weight to zero-option formats.
MSQ and NAT together now command nearly 50% of the paper, so option elimination and guessing do not work; exact derivations are essential.
DBMS and Data Warehousing grew 183% from 2024 (6M to 17M): GATE DA now covers end-to-end data engineering, not only theory.

playbook.body: Probability & Statistics (18M avg), Programming/DSA (15M avg) and General Aptitude (15M fixed) account for 48% of the exam. Flawless execution in this trio alone secures a top-tier percentile before touching other subjects.

With 17M in 2026, DBMS is no minor subject. Data warehousing (star/snowflake), OLAP operations (slice, dice, roll-up), B+ tree depth and transaction serialisation deserve study time equal to Machine Learning.

playbook.rule: Immunise yourself against the zero-option trap
playbook.body: Nearly 50% of the paper has no option-elimination safety net. MSQs need absolute theoretical mastery (one missed choice yields 0), NATs need end-to-end accuracy with exact rounding. Practise numericals without answer choices.

playbook.rule: Linear Algebra is the silent multiplier
playbook.body: Direct questions yield 10–12M, but rank, orthogonality and eigenspaces underpin ML (PCA, SVD, normal equations), optimisation (Hessians, quadratic forms) and statistics.

notes: Marks, ranges and trends above are as printed on pp. 3–6 of the book. Recounting the book's own 195-question bank (pp. 7–64) gives slightly different per-subject marks in places (see the recount table); the book's printed question-type table on p. 4 also does not reconcile with its rows or with the p. 5 yearly mixes (44 MSQ, 46 NAT).
Question-type and 1M/2M counts on this page are recounted from the question bank, which matches the p. 5 yearly mixes exactly (105 MCQ, 44 MSQ, 46 NAT).
